issue_context.title: systemd-nspawn `--suppress-sync=true` also suppresses fd validation in `fsync()`
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

256.5

### Used distribution

Gentoo Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.10.10-gentoo-dist

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-nspawn

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

_No response_

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

`fsync()` (and related calls) returns 0 when passed invalid fd and `--suppress-sync=true` is used.

This is causing CPython's test suite to fail.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Enter a container with `systemd-nspawn --suppress-sync=true`.
2. Compile and run the following program:
    ```c
    #include <stdio.h>
    #include <unistd.h>
    
    int main() {
            printf("fdatasync() = %d\n", fdatasync(-1));
            perror("errno");
            return 0;
    }
    ```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

```sh
fdatasync = 0
errno: Success

(while without --suppress-sync=true, it gives:
fdatasync = -1
errno: Bad file descriptor
)
```

/* test_seccomp_suppress_sync */
src/test/test-seccomp.c:1248: Assertion failed: expected "fdatasync(-1)" to fail with error "Bad file descriptor", but it succeeded

Assertion 'wait_for_terminate_and_check("seccomp_suppress_sync", pid, WAIT_LOG) == EXIT_SUCCESS' failed at src/test/test-seccomp.c:1261, function test_seccomp_suppress_sync(). Aborting.

Of course, the test succeeds when --suppress-sync=no.

Is your systemd-nspawn built with SECCOMP support??

> Hmm? That's exactly the issue here, no? The error clearly shows that fdatasync() unexpectedly succeeded.

When `--suppress-sync=yes`, `fdatasync(-1)` should succeed, and the test case added in #34480 will fail, as the test assumes that no seccomp filter for sync related syscalls are installed and expects the call fails.
When `--suppress-sync=no`, `fdstasync(-1)` should fail, and the test case will succeed as expected.

Anyway, please check the below at first:
> Please check `systemd-nspawn --version` shows `+SECCOMP`.

> When `--suppress-sync=yes`, `fdatasync(-1)` should succeed, and the test case added in #34480 will fail, as the test assumes that no seccomp filter for sync related syscalls are installed and expects the call fails.

In my opinion, it shouldn't succeed. The documentation says that it:

> turns off any form of on-disk file system synchronization for the container payload. This means all system calls such as sync(2), fsync(), syncfs(), ... will execute no operation […].

However, even if the call doesn't do anything, it is supposed to return an appropriate error if called with invalid arguments, according to POSIX.

> Anyway, please check the below at first:
> 
> > Please check `systemd-nspawn --version` shows `+SECCOMP`.

Yes, it does.

```
systemd 256 (256.5)
+PAM +AUDIT -SELINUX -APPARMOR +IMA +SMACK +SECCOMP +GCRYPT +GNUTLS +OPENSSL +ACL +BLKID +CURL +ELFUTILS -FIDO2 +IDN2 -IDN -IPTC +KMOD -LIBCRYPTSETUP -LIBCRYPTSETUP_PLUGINS +LIBFDISK +PCRE2 -PWQUALITY -P11KIT +QRENCODE +TPM2 +BZIP2 +LZ4 +XZ +ZLIB +ZSTD -BPF_FRAMEWORK -XKBCOMMON +UTMP -SYSVINIT +LIBARCHIVE
```

> When --suppress-sync=yes, fdatasync(-1) should succeed

Again, this is what the whole report is about...

Ah, I misunderstood the report.

The behavior is expected. `--suppress-sync=yes` installs seccomp filter for fsync and friends to make they unconditionally succeed. So, even an invalid fd is passed, it succeeds.

I think the original reporter has a point: to minimize unexpected breakages by --suppress-sync= we should probably extend our seccomp filter to return EBADF on negative fds. I mean, the goal with that option is to just speed up things, but from app pov it shouldn't change behaviour as much as possible.

i mean, everything has boundaries: tweaking the seccomp filter to refuse negative fds should be fairly easy. But tweaking it to refuse positive-but-invalid fds would be too much to ask, and simply not implementable via seccomp. But just because we cannot do the latter, we still should do the former.
